metadata.title: Justice Hill is Beginning to Make Some Noise
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens running back Justice Hill was able to find success on the ground during the Week 3 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. He carried the ball five times for 33 yards in the victory over the Cowboys. He averaged 6.6 yards per carry, which is encouraging to see from the veteran back. Overall, Hill is going to have his fantasy value capped as the backup to Derrick Henry. He could see more carries if he continues rushing as he did during Sunday's game. However, the 28-year-old is unlikely to have standalone value moving forward. He could be worth stashing in case Henry goes down at some point.

metadata.title: Justice Hill runs for 33 yards in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Justice Hill carried the ball five times for 33 yards in a 34-31 win over the Cowboys in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Hill averaged 6.6 yards per carry in the exciting win over Dallas in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday. The veteran running back continues to mix in behind starter Derrick Henry, with Week 3 being his most productive game of the season. Hill will not be a strong fantasy option heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Titans.

metadata.title: Justice Hill - Two carries and two targets in loss
metadata.description: Hill rushed twice for six yards and caught two targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
metadata.analysis: Hill was on the field for 27 of the Ravens' 58 offensive snaps. The running back saw usage in both the run and pass offenses, providing a fast contrast to Derrick Henry's bulk. It appears the new Ravens offense wants to utilize Hill at a higher rate, potentially to rest the 32-year-old Henry more frequently.

metadata.title: Justice Hill quiet in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Justice Hill rushed for six yards on two carries in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints.
metadata.analysis: Hill was uninvolved in the passing game and saw his touches drop from Week 1. Fantasy managers should expect Hill to continue to see limited usage as long as Derrick Henry is healthy.

metadata.title: Justice Hill - Sees seven touches in Week 1 victory
metadata.description: Hill turned six carries into 18 yards and added a 10-yard catch during the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Hill saw an uptick in usage in the fourth quarter with the Ravens firmly in control of the game. He played 31 of 68 offensive snaps, which wasn't that far behind bell cow Derrick Henry's 37 snaps, though Hill is firmly entrenched as the Ravens' RB2, with Rasheen Ali being the distant third option. Hill will continue to serve as the change-of-pace back for the Ravens heading into Week 2 against the Saints on Sept. 20.

metadata.title: Justice Hill sees seven touches in Week 1
metadata.description: Justice Hill rushed six times for 18 yards while catching his only target for 10 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Hill operated as more of an afterthought out of the Baltimore backfield, with Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson finishing ahead of the running back in carries. He remains more of a change-of-pace option behind Henry ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

metadata.title: Justice Hill To Have Limited Role In Week 1
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens running back Justice Hill won the backup running back job to Derrick Henry, but his role will be limited with Henry starting the season healthy in Week 1. Hill has shown nice change of pace in the backfield in the past and can catch passes out of the backfield, but with Henry healthy, the bellcow should have a stranglehold on carries in the Ravens' backfield. Hill has big-play explosiveness but he just isn't likely to get a heavy share of carries or targets out of the backfield early on in the season. He is more than capable as a backup back and is worth holding onto in fantasy leagues as a down-the-road target but during the time that Henry is healthy, Hill should have little-to-no consistent role in the offense.

metadata.title: Justice Hill Fits Better as PPR Insurance Than a Week 1 Play
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens running back Justice Hill has a cleaner hold on the No. 2 job than he did earlier this summer, but that still doesn't make him a priority Week 1 add. Rookie Adam Randall is on injured reserve with a designation to return, leaving Hill second behind Derrick Henry and Rasheen Ali third on Baltimore's current depth chart. Hill's value comes from passing downs. He caught 21 passes for 169 yards and a touchdown in 10 games last season, and new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has called him one of the league's best third-down backs. Hill is healthy after last year's neck injury, too. The catch is that he is not an obvious candidate to absorb Henry's entire workload if something happens. Ali could take some early-down work, and Hill sits at RB56 in the current Week 1 rankings. In deeper PPR leagues, he is a reasonable bench stash. In standard 10- or 12-team formats, there are better ways to use the spot.

metadata.title: Justice Hill's Handcuff Value Gets a Boost
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens running back Justice Hill enters Week 1 with a much cleaner path behind Derrick Henry. Rookie Adam Randall was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return during final cuts, leaving Hill and Rasheen Ali as the only other active backs on the initial 53-man roster. Baltimore's own roster breakdown called Hill a prized backup and identified Ali as the No. 3 back. That is a meaningful change after RotoBaller questioned earlier in August whether Randall could eventually become the better two-down handcuff. Hill was limited to 10 games last season by toe and neck injuries, finishing with 93 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 18 carries while adding 21 catches for 169 yards and another score. He still profiles better as a passing-down option than a direct replacement for Henry's massive early-down workload, and Ali could absorb some carries if Henry misses time. For now, though, the depth chart is cleaner. With Randall unavailable for at least four games, Hill opens the year with a stronger claim to Baltimore's No. 2 role.

metadata.title: Justice Hill Listed as RB2 on the Ravens' Depth Chart
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens running back Justice Hill was listed as the No. 2 option behind Derrick Henry on the team's latest unofficial depth chart. It seemed like Adam Randall (undisclosed) and Rasheen Ali were both trending up this preseason, but nevertheless, Hill is holding on to his second-string role for the time being. Hill was the RB37 in PPR leagues in 2024, but he took a step backward when he missed seven games last year. With that being said, Hill is still a very productive pass-catching back who should consistently play on receiving downs. He had 42 catches and 383 receiving yards in his explosive season in 2024, and he should continue to get involved in a new offensive system led by coordinator Declan Doyle, assuming he's able to stay healthy. There's low-end fantasy appeal in PPR leagues here. Hill won't get a significant number of carries regardless of whether Derrick Henry is on the field, but he should maintain a consistent receiving role, which makes him a low-end flex in deeper PPR formats.

metadata.title: Justice Hill - Backing up Henry in 2026
metadata.description: Hill is in line to be the No.2 running back on the Ravens' depth chart to open the 2026 season.
metadata.analysis: The veteran is in the final year of his contract after an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to 10 regular-season games. Hill is also playing under a new coaching staff and an offensive coordinator, so it will be interesting to see whether his role evolves or other options emerge as Derrick Henry's backup. Hill has been healthy for the preseason and hasn't appeared in either preseason game, which is seemingly a good sign for his standing on the depth chart.

metadata.title: Justice Hill Could Lose Handcuff Role to Adam Randall in 2026
metadata.description: Baltimore Ravens running back Justice Hill is coming off a down year in 2025, with 18 carries for 93 yards and two touchdowns, plus 169 yards and one touchdown on 21 receptions. Hill had his lowest carries per game (1.8), rushing yards (9.3), and total attempts per game (3.9) since 2020. While he's been a solid third-down back and special teams player for the team, his 2025 decline could be part of the reason they spent a fifth-round pick on running back Adam Randall. While star running back Derrick Henry will be the workhorse in Baltimore, any injury could mean Randall steps into the two-down back role rather than Hill. Without a clear handcuff role, Hill is likely too low for fantasy relevance in 2026.
